audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Kings / Melakhim Bet Shunammite restoration, Hazael oracle, and Judah/Israel royal transition narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for famine migration, land-restoration petition, Gehazi's testimony, royal restitution, Ben-hadad's illness, Hazael's deception and killing, Elisha's tears over future atrocities, Jehoram and Ahaziah chronology, dynastic intermarriage, Edomite revolt, and war injury.

verses.restored: Elisha spoke to woman whose son he had restored to life, saying, Rise and go, you and your household, and sojourn wherever you can sojourn, for YHWH has called for famine, and it is also coming upon land seven years.

familiar.text: Then spake Elisha unto the woman, whose son he had restored to life, saying, Arise, and go thou and thine household, and sojourn wheresoever thou canst sojourn: for the LORD hath called for a famine; and it shall also come upon the land seven years.

modern.text: Now Elisha had said to the woman whose son he had restored to life, “Arise, you and your household; go and live as a foreigner wherever you can. For the LORD has decreed a seven-year famine, and it has already come to the land.”

original.text: וֶאֱלִישָׁ֡ע דִּבֶּ֣ר אֶל הָאִשָּׁה֩ אֲשֶׁר הֶחֱיָ֨ה אֶת בְּנָ֜הּ לֵאמֹ֗ר ק֤וּמִי וּלְכִי֙ אתי וּבֵיתֵ֔ךְ וְג֖וּרִי בַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר תָּג֑וּרִי כִּֽי קָרָ֤א יְהוָה֙ לָֽרָעָ֔ב וְגַם בָּ֥א אֶל הָאָ֖רֶץ שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִֽים

verses.restored: The woman rose and did according to word of man of Divine; she went, she and her household, and sojourned in land of Philistines seven years.

familiar.text: And the woman arose, and did after the saying of the man of God: and she went with her household, and sojourned in the land of the Philistines seven years.

modern.text: So the woman had proceeded to do as the man of God had instructed. And she and her household lived as foreigners for seven years in the land of the Philistines.

original.text: וַתָּ֨קָם֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה וַתַּ֕עַשׂ כִּדְבַ֖ר אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַתֵּ֤לֶךְ הִיא֙ וּבֵיתָ֔הּ וַתָּ֥גָר בְּאֶֽרֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִֽים

verses.restored: It was at end of seven years that woman returned from land of Philistines and went out to cry to king for her house and her field.

familiar.text: And it came to pass at the seven years’ end, that the woman returned out of the land of the Philistines: and she went forth to cry unto the king for her house and for her land.

modern.text: At the end of seven years, when the woman returned from the land of the Philistines, she went to the king to appeal for her house and her land.

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י מִקְצֵה֙ שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֔ים וַתָּ֥שָׁב הָאִשָּׁ֖ה מֵאֶ֣רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַתֵּצֵא֙ לִצְעֹ֣ק אֶל הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֶל בֵּיתָ֖הּ וְאֶל שָׂדָֽהּ

verses.restored: King was speaking to Gehazi servant of man of Divine, saying, Recount to me, please, all great things Elisha has done.

familiar.text: And the king talked with Gehazi the servant of the man of God, saying, Tell me, I pray thee, all the great things that Elisha hath done.

modern.text: Now the king had been speaking to Gehazi, the servant of the man of God, saying, “Please relate to me all the great things Elisha has done.”

original.text: וְהַמֶּ֗לֶךְ מְדַבֵּר֙ אֶל גֵּ֣חֲזִ֔י נַ֥עַר אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים לֵאמֹ֑ר סַפְּרָה נָּ֣א לִ֔י אֵ֥ת כָּל הַגְּדֹל֖וֹת אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֥ה אֱלִישָֽׁע

verses.restored: It was, as he was recounting to king how he restored dead one to life, that look, woman whose son he restored to life cried to king for her house and field. Gehazi said, My lord king, this is the woman, and this is her son whom Elisha restored to life.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, as he was telling the king how he had restored a dead body to life, that, behold, the woman, whose son he had restored to life, cried to the king for her house and for her land. And Gehazi said, My lord, O king, this is the woman, and this is her son, whom Elisha restored to life.

modern.text: And Gehazi was telling the king how Elisha had brought the dead back to life. Just then the woman whose son Elisha had revived came to appeal to the king for her house and her land. So Gehazi said, “My lord the king, this is the woman, and this is the son Elisha restored to life.”

original.text: וַ֠יְהִי ה֥וּא מְסַפֵּ֣ר לַמֶּלֶךְ֮ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר הֶחֱיָ֣ה אֶת הַמֵּת֒ וְהִנֵּ֨ה הָאִשָּׁ֜ה אֲשֶׁר הֶחֱיָ֤ה אֶת בְּנָהּ֙ צֹעֶ֣קֶת אֶל הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ עַל בֵּיתָ֖הּ וְעַל שָׂדָ֑הּ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר גֵּֽחֲזִי֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ זֹ֚את הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה וְזֶה בְּנָ֖הּ אֲשֶׁר הֶחֱיָ֥ה אֱלִישָֽׁע

verses.restored: King asked woman, and she recounted to him. King appointed to her one officer, saying, Restore all belonging to her and all produce of field from day she left land until now.

familiar.text: And when the king asked the woman, she told him. So the king appointed unto her a certain officer, saying, Restore all that was hers, and all the fruits of the field since the day that she left the land, even until now.

modern.text: When the king asked the woman, she confirmed it. So the king appointed for her an officer, saying, “Restore all that was hers, along with all the proceeds of the field from the day that she left the country until now.” Hazael Murders Ben-hadad

original.text: וַיִּשְׁאַ֥ל הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ לָאִשָּׁ֖ה וַתְּסַפֶּר ל֑וֹ וַיִּתֶּן לָ֣הּ הַמֶּלֶךְ֩ סָרִ֨יס אֶחָ֜ד לֵאמֹ֗ר הָשֵׁ֤יב אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר לָהּ֙ וְאֵת֙ כָּל תְּבוּאֹ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה מִיּ֛וֹם עָזְבָ֥ה אֶת הָאָ֖רֶץ וְעַד עָֽתָּה

verses.restored: Elisha came to Damascus, and Ben-hadad king of Aram was sick. It was told to him, saying, Man of Divine has come here.

familiar.text: And Elisha came to Damascus; and Benhadad the king of Syria was sick; and it was told him, saying, The man of God is come hither.

modern.text: Then Elisha came to Damascus while Ben-hadad king of Aram was sick, and the king was told, “The man of God has come here.”

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֤א אֱלִישָׁע֙ דַּמֶּ֔שֶׂק וּבֶן הֲדַ֥ד מֶֽלֶךְ אֲרָ֖ם חֹלֶ֑ה וַיֻּגַּד ל֣וֹ לֵאמֹ֔ר בָּ֛א אִ֥ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים עַד הֵֽנָּה

verses.restored: King said to Hazael, Take a gift in your hand and go to meet man of Divine, and inquire of YHWH through him, saying, Shall I recover from this sickness?

familiar.text: And the king said unto Hazael, Take a present in thine hand, and go, meet the man of God, and enquire of the LORD by him, saying, Shall I recover of this disease?

modern.text: So the king said to Hazael, “Take a gift in your hand, go to meet the man of God, and inquire of the LORD through him, ‘Will I recover from this illness?’”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶל חֲזָהאֵ֗ל קַ֤ח בְּיָֽדְךָ֙ מִנְחָ֔ה וְלֵ֕ךְ לִקְרַ֖את אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְדָרַשְׁתָּ֨ אֶת יְהוָ֤ה מֵֽאוֹתוֹ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הַאֶחְיֶ֖ה מֵחֳלִ֥י זֶֽה

verses.restored: Hazael went to meet him and took gift in his hand, every good thing of Damascus, burden of forty camels. He came and stood before him and said, Your son Ben-hadad king of Aram sent me to you, saying, Shall I recover from this sickness?

familiar.text: So Hazael went to meet him, and took a present with him, even of every good thing of Damascus, forty camels’ burden, and came and stood before him, and said, Thy son Benhadad king of Syria hath sent me to thee, saying, Shall I recover of this disease?

modern.text: So Hazael went to meet Elisha, taking with him a gift of forty camel loads of every good thing from Damascus. And he went in and stood before him and said, “Your son Ben-hadad king of Aram has sent me to ask, ‘Will I recover from this illness?’”

original.text: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ חֲזָאֵל֮ לִקְרָאתוֹ֒ וַיִּקַּ֨ח מִנְחָ֤ה בְיָדוֹ֙ וְכָל ט֣וּב דַּמֶּ֔שֶׂק מַשָּׂ֖א אַרְבָּעִ֣ים גָּמָ֑ל וַיָּבֹא֙ וַיַּעֲמֹ֣ד לְפָנָ֔יו וַיֹּ֗אמֶר בִּנְךָ֨ בֶן הֲדַ֤ד מֶֽלֶךְ אֲרָם֙ שְׁלָחַ֤נִי אֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הַאֶחְיֶ֖ה מֵחֳלִ֥י זֶֽה

verses.restored: Elisha said to him, Go, say to him, Recovering, you shall recover; yet YHWH has shown me that dying, he shall die.

familiar.text: And Elisha said unto him, Go, say unto him, Thou mayest certainly recover: howbeit the LORD hath shewed me that he shall surely die.

modern.text: Elisha answered, “Go and tell him, ‘You will surely recover.’ But the LORD has shown me that in fact he will die.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ אֱלִישָׁ֔ע לֵ֥ךְ אֱמָר לא חָיֹ֣ה תִחְיֶ֑ה וְהִרְאַ֥נִי יְהוָ֖ה כִּֽי מ֥וֹת יָמֽוּת

verses.restored: He fixed his face and set it until shame, and man of Divine wept.

familiar.text: And he settled his countenance stedfastly, until he was ashamed: and the man of God wept.

modern.text: Elisha fixed his gaze steadily on him until Hazael became uncomfortable. Then the man of God began to weep.

original.text: וַיַּעֲמֵ֥ד אֶת פָּנָ֖יו וַיָּ֣שֶׂם עַד בֹּ֑שׁ וַיֵּ֖בְךְּ אִ֥ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִֽים

verses.restored: Hazael said, Why is my lord weeping? He said, Because I know evil you will do to children of Israel: their fortified places you will send into fire, their young men you will kill by sword, their little ones you will dash, and their pregnant women you will rip open.

familiar.text: And Hazael said, Why weepeth my lord? And he answered, Because I know the evil that thou wilt do unto the children of Israel: their strong holds wilt thou set on fire, and their young men wilt thou slay with the sword, and wilt dash their children, and rip up their women with child.

modern.text: “Why is my lord weeping?” asked Hazael. “Because I know the evil you will do to the Israelites,” Elisha replied. “You will set fire to their fortresses, kill their young men with the sword, dash their little ones to pieces, and rip open their pregnant women.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר חֲזָאֵ֔ל מַדּ֖וּעַ אֲדֹנִ֣י בֹכֶ֑ה וַיֹּ֡אמֶר כִּֽי יָדַ֡עְתִּי אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשֶׂה֩ לִבְנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל רָעָ֗ה מִבְצְרֵיהֶ֞ם תְּשַׁלַּ֤ח בָּאֵשׁ֙ וּבַחֻֽרֵיהֶם֙ בַּחֶ֣רֶב תַּהֲרֹ֔ג וְעֹלְלֵיהֶ֣ם תְּרַטֵּ֔שׁ וְהָרֹתֵיהֶ֖ם תְּבַקֵּֽעַ

verses.restored: Hazael said, But what is your servant, the dog, that he should do this great thing? Elisha said, YHWH has shown me you as king over Aram.

familiar.text: And Hazael said, But what, is thy servant a dog, that he should do this great thing? And Elisha answered, The LORD hath shewed me that thou shalt be king over Syria.

modern.text: “But how could your servant, a mere dog, do such a monstrous thing?” said Hazael. And Elisha answered, “The LORD has shown me that you will be king over Aram.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר חֲזָהאֵ֔ל כִּ֣י מָ֤ה עַבְדְּךָ֙ הַכֶּ֔לֶב כִּ֣י יַעֲשֶׂ֔ה הַדָּבָ֥ר הַגָּד֖וֹל הַזֶּ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלִישָׁ֔ע הִרְאַ֧נִי יְהוָ֛ה אֹתְךָ֖ מֶ֥לֶךְ עַל אֲרָֽם

verses.restored: He went from Elisha and came to his lord. He said to him, What did Elisha say to you? He said, He told me, Recovering, you shall recover.

familiar.text: So he departed from Elisha, and came to his master; who said to him, What said Elisha to thee? And he answered, He told me that thou shouldest surely recover.

modern.text: So Hazael left Elisha and went to his master, who asked him, “What did Elisha say to you?” And he replied, “He told me that you would surely recover.”

original.text: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ מֵאֵ֣ת אֱלִישָׁ֗ע וַיָּבֹא֙ אֶל אֲדֹנָ֔יו וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ מָֽה אָמַ֥ר לְךָ֖ אֱלִישָׁ֑ע וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אָ֥מַר לִ֖י חָיֹ֥ה תִחְיֶֽה

verses.restored: It was on next day that he took coverlet, dipped it in water, spread it over his face, and he died. Hazael reigned in his place.

familiar.text: And it came to pass on the morrow, that he took a thick cloth, and dipped it in water, and spread it on his face, so that he died: and Hazael reigned in his stead.

modern.text: But the next day Hazael took a thick cloth, dipped it in water, and spread it over the king’s face. So Ben-hadad died, and Hazael reigned in his place. Jehoram Reigns in Judah (2 Chronicles 21:1–7)

original.text: וַיְהִ֣י מִֽמָּחֳרָ֗ת וַיִּקַּ֤ח הַמַּכְבֵּר֙ וַיִּטְבֹּ֣ל בַּמַּ֔יִם וַיִּפְרֹ֥שׂ עַל פָּנָ֖יו וַיָּמֹ֑ת וַיִּמְלֹ֥ךְ חֲזָהאֵ֖ל תַּחְתָּֽיו

verses.restored: In fifth year of Joram son of Ahab king of Israel, while Jehoshaphat was king of Judah, Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah began to reign.

familiar.text: And in the fifth year of Joram the son of Ahab king of Israel, Jehoshaphat being then king of Judah, Jehoram the son of Je hoshaphat king of Judah began to reign.

modern.text: In the fifth year of the reign of Joram son of Ahab over Israel, Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat succeeded his father as king of Judah.

original.text: וּבִשְׁנַ֣ת חָמֵ֗שׁ לְיוֹרָ֤ם בֶּן אַחְאָב֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וִיהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה מָלַ֛ךְ יְהוֹרָ֥ם בֶּן יְהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה

verses.restored: Thirty-two years old was he when he became king, and eight years he reigned in Jerusalem.

familiar.text: Thirty and two years old was he when he began to reign; and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.

modern.text: Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem eight years.

original.text: בֶּן שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וּשְׁתַּ֛יִם שָׁנָ֖ה הָיָ֣ה בְמָלְכ֑וֹ וּשְׁמֹנֶ֣ה שנה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם

verses.restored: He walked in way of kings of Israel, as house of Ahab did, for daughter of Ahab was his wife; he did evil in eyes of YHWH.

familiar.text: And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as did the house of Ahab: for the daughter of Ahab was his wife: and he did evil in the sight of the LORD.

modern.text: And Jehoram walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab had done. For he married a daughter of Ahab and did evil in the sight of the LORD.

original.text: וַיֵּ֜לֶךְ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ מַלְכֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשׂוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית אַחְאָ֔ב כִּ֚י בַּת אַחְאָ֔ב הָֽיְתָה לּ֖וֹ לְאִשָּׁ֑ה וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Yet YHWH was unwilling to destroy Judah for sake of David his servant, as he had spoken to give him a lamp for his sons all days.

familiar.text: Yet the LORD would not destroy Judah for David his servant’s sake, as he promised him to give him alway a light, and to his children.

modern.text: Yet for the sake of His servant David, the LORD was unwilling to destroy Judah, since He had promised to maintain a lamp for David and his descendants forever. Edom and Libnah Rebel (2 Chronicles 21:8–11)

original.text: וְלֹֽא אָבָ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לְהַשְׁחִ֣ית אֶת יְהוּדָ֔ה לְמַ֖עַן דָּוִ֣ד עַבְדּ֑וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר אָֽמַר ל֗וֹ לָתֵ֨ת ל֥וֹ נִ֛יר לְבָנָ֖יו כָּל הַיָּמִֽים

verses.restored: In his days Edom revolted from under hand of Judah and made a king over themselves.

familiar.text: In his days Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah, and made a king over themselves.

modern.text: In the days of Jehoram, Edom rebelled against the hand of Judah and appointed their own king.

original.text: בְּיָמָיו֙ פָּשַׁ֣ע אֱד֔וֹם מִתַּ֖חַת יַד יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיַּמְלִ֥כוּ עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם מֶֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: Joram crossed to Zair, and all chariots with him. He rose by night and struck Edomites surrounding him and commanders of chariots, but people fled to their tents.

familiar.text: So Joram went over to Zair, and all the chariots with him: and he rose by night, and smote the Edomites which compassed him about, and the captains of the chariots: and the people fled into their tents.

modern.text: So Jehoram crossed over to Zair with all his chariots. When the Edomites surrounded him and his chariot commanders, he rose up and attacked by night. His troops, however, fled to their homes.

original.text: וַיַּעֲבֹ֤ר יוֹרָם֙ צָעִ֔ירָה וְכָל הָרֶ֖כֶב עִמּ֑וֹ וַֽיְהִי ה֞וּא קָ֣ם לַ֗יְלָה וַיַּכֶּ֨ה אֶת אֱד֜וֹם הַסֹּבֵ֤יב אֵלָיו֙ וְאֵת֙ שָׂרֵ֣י הָרֶ֔כֶב וַיָּ֥נָס הָעָ֖ם לְאֹהָלָֽיו

verses.restored: Edom revolted from under hand of Judah to this day. Then Libnah revolted at that time.

familiar.text: Yet Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah unto this day. Then Libnah revolted at the same time.

modern.text: So to this day Edom has been in rebellion against the hand of Judah. Likewise, Libnah rebelled at the same time.

original.text: וַיִּפְשַׁ֣ע אֱד֗וֹם מִתַּ֨חַת֙ יַד יְהוּדָ֔ה עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה אָ֛ז תִּפְשַׁ֥ע לִבְנָ֖ה בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִֽיא

verses.restored: Remaining matters of Joram and all he did, are they not written in scroll of matters of days of kings of Judah?

familiar.text: And the rest of the acts of Joram, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

modern.text: As for the rest of the acts of Jehoram, along with all his accomplishments, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?

original.text: וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י יוֹרָ֖ם וְכָל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲלֽוֹא הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה

verses.restored: Joram lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in city of David; Ahaziah his son reigned in his place.

familiar.text: And Joram slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David: and Ahaziah his son reigned in his stead.

modern.text: And Jehoram rested with his fathers and was buried with them in the City of David. And his son Ahaziah reigned in his place. Ahaziah Reigns in Judah (2 Chronicles 22:1–7)

original.text: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב יוֹרָם֙ עִם אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּקָּבֵ֥ר עִם אֲבֹתָ֖יו בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֑ד וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֲחַזְיָ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו

verses.restored: In twelfth year of Joram son of Ahab king of Israel, Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah began to reign.

familiar.text: In the twelfth year of Joram the son of Ahab king of Israel did Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah begin to reign.

modern.text: In the twelfth year of the reign of Joram son of Ahab over Israel, Ahaziah son of Jehoram became king of Judah.

original.text: בִּשְׁנַת֙ שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה לְיוֹרָ֥ם בֶּן אַחְאָ֖ב מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מָלַ֛ךְ אֲחַזְיָ֥הוּ בֶן יְהוֹרָ֖ם מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה

verses.restored: Twenty-two years old was Ahaziah when he became king, and one year he reigned in Jerusalem. Name of his mother was Athaliah daughter/granddaughter of Omri king of Israel.

familiar.text: Two and twenty years old was Ahaziah when he began to reign; and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Athaliah, the daughter of Omri king of Israel.

modern.text: Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem one year. His mother’s name was Athaliah, the granddaughter of Omri king of Israel.

verses.restored: He walked in way of house of Ahab and did evil in eyes of YHWH like house of Ahab, for he was son-in-law of house of Ahab.

familiar.text: And he walked in the way of the house of Ahab, and did evil in the sight of the LORD, as did the house of Ahab: for he was the son in law of the house of Ahab.

modern.text: And Ahaziah walked in the ways of the house of Ahab and did evil in the sight of the LORD like the house of Ahab, for he was a son-in-law of the house of Ahab.

verses.restored: He went with Joram son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-gilead, and Arameans struck Joram.

familiar.text: And he went with Joram the son of Ahab to the war against Hazael king of Syria in Ramothgilead; and the Syrians wounded Joram.

modern.text: Then Ahaziah went with Joram son of Ahab to fight against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-gilead, and the Arameans wounded Joram.

original.text: וַיֵּ֜לֶךְ אֶת יוֹרָ֣ם בֶּן אַחְאָ֗ב לַמִּלְחָמָ֛ה עִם חֲזָהאֵ֥ל מֶֽלֶךְ אֲרָ֖ם בְּרָמֹ֣ת גִּלְעָ֑ד וַיַּכּ֥וּ אֲרַמִּ֖ים אֶת יוֹרָֽם

verses.restored: King Joram returned to be healed at Jezreel from wounds Arameans struck him at Ramah when he fought Hazael king of Aram. Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Joram son of Ahab at Jezreel because he was sick/wounded.

familiar.text: And king Joram went back to be healed in Jezreel of the wounds which the Syrians had given him at Ramah, when he fought against Hazael king of Syria. And Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Joram the son of Ahab in Jezreel, because he was sick.

modern.text: So King Joram returned to Jezreel to recover from the wounds that the Arameans had inflicted on him at Ramah when he fought against Hazael king of Aram. Then Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to Jezreel to visit Joram son of Ahab, because Joram had been wounded.

translation_notes: The Shunammite woman migrates with her household because of famine and later petitions for restoration of house, field, and accumulated produce. Displacement does not erase property claims.
Her case is heard directly, verified, and remedied with back produce. This is restitution, not charity.
Gehazi's appearance after chapter 5 creates chronological and compositional questions, especially if his skin disease is assumed continuous; the text should not force a simplistic timeline.
Ben-hadad's sickness is not moral failure. The danger lies in succession politics and Hazael's actions, not illness itself.
Elisha's statement to Hazael is textually and morally difficult: the king may recover from the illness but will still die. Hazael reports only the reassuring half.
Elisha weeps before naming Hazael's future atrocities. Prophetic knowledge does not equal approval, and foreknowledge does not remove Hazael's responsibility.
The listed atrocities include burning cities, killing young men, dashing children, and ripping open pregnant women. These are war crimes and must never be sanctified by prophecy.
Hazael's 'dog' language is self-abasement and disbelief, not permission to dehumanize people through animal comparisons.
Hazael kills Ben-hadad by suffocation with a wet coverlet. The narrative must not become instruction or apologetics for political assassination.
Royal marriage connections are narrated as dynastic influence, but women such as Athaliah and Ahab's daughter must not be made scapegoats for men's policies.
Edom's revolt is a subject people's political break from Judah; imperial loss is not automatically moral chaos.
Regnal synchronisms and Athaliah's relation to Omri vary in interpretation and require textual-chronological audit.
safety_note: Do not blame famine migrants, erase displaced owners, stigmatize illness, glorify assassination, or treat prophecy as approval of atrocity. Preserve the Shunammite woman's right to full restitution, Elisha's grief, Hazael's accountability, the humanity of Edomites and Arameans, and the moral horror of violence against children and pregnant people.
